transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I can’t shake this feeling that I’m useless now and just letting everyone down since my fall. Ever since my knee procedure, I've had to step back from all my usual activities, and I just feel like a complete burden to the people who were counting on me.
Has this persistent feeling of being a burden started only after your knee procedure, or did you feel this way even before the injury?

No, I never felt this way before the injury; I was always highly active, independent, and busy helping others. These feelings only started a couple of weeks after my knee procedure, once it became clear I wasn't bouncing back like I'd hoped. Now, because I can't do any of the things I used to, I just feel like dead weight.
Can you tell me if there have been any other major life changes or stressors, besides the knee injury, that have been weighing on you recently?

No, there hasn't been anything else. It is really just this knee injury and the sudden loss of my active lifestyle, my independence, and my roles in the community. That is the sole thing weighing so heavily on me right now.
Beyond these feelings about your injury, have you also been experiencing other symptoms like significant changes in your appetite, trouble sleeping, or difficulty concentrating?

Yes, I've been struggling with all of those lately. I have to force myself to eat, usually only managing a piece of toast or yogurt, and at night I lie awake worrying before waking up exhausted around 4 a.m. My mind feels so foggy too; I lose my train of thought constantly and get completely overwhelmed just trying to decide what to wear.

Do you feel that your low mood and lack of motivation are exclusively focused on your recovery and the limitations caused by your knee, or do you find that these feelings have begun to persist even when you aren't thinking about your injury?

While the knee injury definitely started all of this, the low mood has turned into a constant, heavy cloud that hangs over me all day. Even when I'm not actively thinking about my recovery—like when I'm just sitting staring at the TV—I still feel this steady, blank indifference and a heavy fatigue that won't go away. It just feels like it's there all the time now, regardless of what I'm doing.

If your knee were to heal completely tomorrow and you were physically capable again, do you feel that your current sense of hopelessness and lack of interest in things would immediately resolve, or do you feel that this 'heavy cloud' would likely persist regardless of your physical recovery?

I'm not really sure how to answer that. This heavy cloud feels so overwhelming and constant right now that it's hard to even imagine what it would feel like if my knee healed, or whether this feeling would actually go away.

Do you still find yourself capable of feeling genuine pleasure or joy when something positive happens, or does this 'heavy cloud' prevent you from feeling any enjoyment at all, even in moments unrelated to your injury?

Yes, the heavy cloud really prevents me from feeling any joy at all. I just feel a blank indifference toward the things that used to light me up, like my workshops, hiking, or even my gardening. Instead of finding enjoyment in anything, I just sit in front of the TV and feel nothing.

Have you noticed any times in the last few weeks where you felt completely unable to enjoy anything at all, even for a short period, or do you still have occasional moments where you can genuinely laugh or feel happy?

No, I don't really have those moments of genuine happiness or laughter anymore. I just feel a complete, blank indifference toward everything that used to bring me joy. Instead of joining in, I just sit in front of the TV feeling completely empty.
